USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the completed $50B Section 301 package in place and keep List 3 fully teed up, but do not implement the $200B list (and especially not at 25 percent) this week. Use the just-closed comment process and the unused $200B threat as leverage in talks that demand structural IP, tech-transfer, and industrial-policy changes, not another May-style purchase pledge. If Beijing again offers only volume buys and no structural movement, implement List 3 later at 10 percent, not 25 percent.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is roughly balanced, not high and not a clear opportunity. The U.S. still has unused tariff room China cannot match dollar-for-dollar (U.S. goods imports from China far exceed U.S. goods exports to China; Beijing published a $60B counter to List 3, not $200B). The domestic macro is not flashing distress: Michigan sentiment is 100.1, industrial production is rising, and VIX is about 13.9. China is under more pressure: yuan down roughly 8 percent since spring (DEXCHUS 6.33 to 6.83), industrial production growth slowing (107.0 to 105.8), reserves edging down. Offsetting costs that keep this from reading as a U.S. opportunity: China already matched the $50B and aimed it at soy, autos, and aircraft; soybean prices fell from about $11 to under $9; China largely halted new bean purchases; USDA announced up to $12B in farm aid on 27 Aug. U.S. goods exports to China are down while imports have been front-loaded, so the goods deficit has widened. Action stays at negotiate because the May 19 purchase-only truce collapsed by May 29 without IP concessions; List 3 comments just closed on 5 Sep so firing 25 percent immediately would hit consumer goods into peak shipping and invite the $60B Chinese list into harvest; only low-level Malpass-Wang talks are underway, so unused List 3 leverage is more valuable than an immediate hike.
key_factors: $50B Section 301 already in force both ways; List 3 ($200B) comment period just closed, not yet imposed
U.S. macro still healthy; China showing FX pressure, slower IP, modest reserve decline
Farm-belt retaliation is the main U.S. cost: soy prices under $9, China halted new purchases, $12B USDA aid
Bilateral imbalance worsening: imports from China front-loaded, exports to China down, goods deficit wider
May 19 purchase-only truce collapsed within 10 days; Section 301 IP issues remain unaddressed
China cannot match List 3 dollar-for-dollar; unused U.S. tariff room is remaining leverage
Low-level talks only; immediate 25 percent List 3 would hit consumers into peak season without a structural Chinese offer

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR Section 301 report finds China IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable; memorandum directs tariffs, WTO case, investment restrictions.
Joint statement: China agrees to significantly increase purchases. Mnuchin says trade war is on hold.
White House proceeds with Section 301 25 percent tariffs on about $50B. Truce collapses.
List 1 takes effect: US 25 percent on about $34B; China matching retaliation same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: about $200B of Chinese imports for additional 10 percent tariff.
USTR considering raising proposed List 3 rate from 10 percent to 25 percent.
List 2 takes effect: US 25 percent on about $16B; China matching retaliation.
Michigan Consumer Sentiment 100.1 on 2018-09-01, up from 96.2 in August.
VIX 13.91 on 2018-09-05; equity vol not pricing a crisis.
U.S. goods imports from China $38.2B in Apr to $49.9B in Sep, +30.6 percent.
U.S. goods exports to China $10.5B in Apr to $9.7B in Sep, -7.4 percent.
CNY weakened from about 6.33 in mid-March to 6.827 on 2018-09-05.
China industrial production YoY index eased from 107.0 in Apr to 105.8 in Sep.
US threatened third round on $200bn, possibly 25 percent. China said it would respond on $60bn. Low-level talks in Washington; hopes not high.
Soybean prices from about $11 to less than $9. China essentially halted new soybean purchases.
USDA announced up to $12 billion in programs to offset retaliatory damage.
On 3 Aug China released a $60 billion retaliation list if Washington proceeds with the $200 billion action.
USTR held public hearings 20-27 Aug 2018 on proposed tariffs on approximately $200 billion of Chinese products.
